events.title: Nebuchadnezzar II's Babylon
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar II makes Babylon the world's most impressive city with the Ishtar Gate, Hanging Gardens, and enormous temples. The city may have had around 200,000 inhabitants.

events.title: Buddha
events.description: Siddhartha Gautama, later known as Buddha, lives and teaches in India. He founded Buddhism with his teachings on suffering, enlightenment, and the Eightfold Path.

events.title: Confucius
events.description: Kongzi (Confucius) lives and teaches in China. His teachings on morality, social order, respect for parents, and just governance shape Chinese culture for millennia.

events.title: Laozi and Taoism
events.description: Laozi, traditionally credited with the "Tao Te Ching", lays the foundation for Taoism with its teachings on the Tao (the Way), wu wei (non-action), and harmony with nature.

events.title: Cyrus the Great Founders the Persian Empire
events.description: Cyrus II of Persia defeats the Medes, Lydians, and Babylonians and establishes the Achaemenid Empire—the largest empire to date.

events.title: The Cyrus Cylinder
events.description: After conquering Babylon, Cyrus issues a decree (the Cyrus Cylinder) allowing deported peoples to return home and rebuild their temples. Often called the first human rights document.

events.title: Fall of Babylon
events.description: Cyrus the Great conquers Babylon in 539 BC, seemingly without battle. The Neo-Babylonian Empire falls and is replaced by the Persian one.

events.title: Greek Philosophy Begins
events.description: Thales, Anaximander, and Heraclitus in Ionia begin seeking natural explanations for the world, marking the start of Western philosophy and science.

events.title: Pythagoras
events.description: Pythagoras establishes his philosophical and mathematical school in Croton (Southern Italy). His theorem and number mysticism have lasting influence.

events.title: The Roman Republic
events.description: Rome overthrows its last king and establishes a republic with two consuls, a senate, and an assembly of the people. A system of government that lasts for nearly 500 years.

events.title: The Axial Age
events.description: Philosopher Karl Jaspers' term for this period: independently of each other, major religious and philosophical traditions emerge in China, India, Persia, and Greece—a spiritual revolution in human thought.
